author: Claude (Orchestrator) — review R1 repair
notes: S5 numeric optimization uses the parent's ALREADY-WIRED strategy inputs; no new numeric inputs are introduced. Each lever is optimized on the frozen S3/S4 pattern-filter combination. This grid is registered evidence; the OPT_CENSUS/S5 ledger owns declared_trial_count.

selection_rule.consistency: >= 2/3 of selection years improve, each by >= +5% relative
selection_rule.walk_forward: anchored/expanding, minimum window 3 years, selection years 2019-2025, test years 2022-2025
selection_rule.activity_floor: >= 10 distinct entry trading days per scored year (pro-rata for partial years); a break in ANY year makes the value inadmissible, excluded BEFORE return is measured
selection_rule.pick: plateau median, never the best value (DL-088 section 3)

control_discipline.cells_per_trial: one lever varied per trial; all other levers held at parent value (DL-088 AI_PARAM)
control_discipline.mandatory_control: each lever's parent_value is a required candidate and the control cell
control_discipline.no_take_profit_lever: the parent has no TP mechanic; req.tp is fixed at 0.0, so no TP parameter exists to optimize

trial_accounting.note: 5 + 5 + 4 candidate cells. The all-parent control config is mechanically shared across levers and is measured once. declared_trial_count for the Q16 DSR deflation is written by the S5 ledger per plan section S5 (154 pattern trials + numeric trials); this file does not set it.

parameters.name: strategy_max_range_atr_mult
parameters.rationale: This multiple is both the upper edge of the ATR(14,H1) range-admission band and the hard SL cap (parent SPEC section 2). Lowering it rejects the widest overnight ranges — starving the strategy of exactly the high-volatility breakout days Balke's method targets; raising it admits ranges whose ATR-multiple stop is uneconomically wide, inflating per-trade risk and MaxDD. A symmetric step-0.5 ladder brackets the parent 2.5 with two values on each side so a return_to_maxdd plateau (if any) can be identified and its median taken, rather than chasing a single best point.

parameters.name: strategy_trail_trigger_r
parameters.rationale: Profit in R before the prior-two-bar swing trail engages (parent SPEC section 2). A smaller trigger locks the swing stop earlier, protecting open profit but cutting continuation runs on strong breakout days; a larger trigger lets the runner extend before trailing, at the cost of giving back more on reversals. return_to_maxdd is directly sensitive to where trailing begins. A tight symmetric step-0.25 ladder centered on the parent 1.0 (two below, two above) reads the local plateau around the parent without leaving the swing-trail's economically meaningful neighbourhood.

parameters.name: strategy_range_end_hour

bounds.constraint: must exceed strategy_range_start_hour (3); bars_in_range must reach (end - start)

parameters.rationale: First GMT+3 hour after the accumulation range; with strategy_range_start_hour fixed at 3 this sets both the range width and the order-placement hour. The parent value 6 is Balke's exact 3-hour window (03:00-06:00). The ladder spans one shorter window (5 = 2-hour range, earlier entry on a tighter range) through the ancestor QM5_9936's 5-hour width (8), which is the card-grounded economic range: a longer window builds a wider, more-tested range with fewer but higher-quality breakouts and a later entry, a shorter window gives earlier entries on a thinner range. A 1-hour window (end = 4) is excluded as economically degenerate — it collapses the range to a single H1 bar's high/low, defeating the multi-hour accumulation the strategy relies on.
